@@ -0,0 +1,133 @@
+---
+title: Configure home network support for Microsoft Entra Private Access
+description: Learn how to configure home network support so users can access local resources while Microsoft Entra Private Access remains enabled.
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 10/13/2026
+ms.subservice: entra-private-access
+ms.reviewer: katabish
+ai-usage: ai-assisted
+# Customer intent: As an administrator, I want to configure home network support so users can access directly connected local resources without disconnecting Microsoft Entra Private Access.
+---
+
+# Configure home network support for Microsoft Entra Private Access (preview)
+
+Home network support in Microsoft Entra Private Access helps users connect to resources on their directly connected local network while Private Access remains enabled. For example, users can connect to a home printer, router, wireless display adapter, or locally hosted virtual machine without disconnecting the Global Secure Access client.
+
+This capability is useful when a Private Access application segment overlaps the user's local subnet. An organization might configure a broad private IP range, such as `10.0.0.0/8` or `192.168.0.0/16`, while a user's home network uses an address within the same range. Without home network support, the Global Secure Access client can acquire traffic intended for the local resource and route it through Private Access, breaking local access.
+
+When **Prefer Local Network** is enabled, the client identifies the directly connected local subnet and sends matching traffic directly to the local network.
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> Home network support is currently in preview. This information relates to a prerelease product that might be substantially modified before release. Microsoft makes no warranties, expressed or implied, with respect to the information provided here. For more information, see the [Microsoft Entra preview terms](https://azure.microsoft.com/support/legal/preview-supplemental-terms/).
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+Before you begin, make sure you have:
+
+- A Microsoft Entra Private Access or Microsoft Entra Suite license.
+- A configured and enabled Private Access traffic forwarding profile.
+- A supported Global Secure Access client with Private Access connected.
+- The [Global Secure Access Administrator](../identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#global-secure-access-administrator) role to manage traffic forwarding profiles.
+
+## How home network support works
+
+The Global Secure Access client uses the IP address and subnet mask assigned to a network adapter to calculate the directly connected local subnet.
+
+For example, if an adapter has the address `192.168.4.69/22`, the calculated local subnet is `192.168.4.0/22`. When **Prefer Local Network** is enabled, traffic to a destination in that subnet remains on the local network instead of being acquired by Private Access.
+
+Home network support affects Private Access traffic only. It doesn't bypass Microsoft traffic or internet traffic forwarding policies.
+
+## Enable home network support
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com/) as a Global Secure Access Administrator.
+1. Browse to **Global Secure Access** > **Connect** > **Traffic forwarding**.
+1. Switch to the new v2 experience, if you haven't already.
+1. Open the Private Access traffic forwarding profile that applies to the target users.
+1. Enable the **Allow local subnet bypass** setting.
+1. Save the profile.
+
+:::image type="content" source="media/how-to-configure-home-network-support/allow-local-subnet-bypass.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the Private Access traffic forwarding profile Basics page with Allow local subnet bypass enabled.":::
+
+After the updated profile reaches the client, the user can manage the local network preference from the Global Secure Access client.
+
+## Enable Prefer Local Network on the client
+
+1. Open the Global Secure Access client.
+1. Select **Settings**.
+1. Turn on **Prefer Local Network**.
+1. Connect to the local resource again.
+
+:::image type="content" source="media/how-to-configure-home-network-support/prefer-local-network.png" alt-text="Screenshot of Global Secure Access client Settings with Prefer Local Network turned on.":::
+
+The preference remains in effect as the device changes networks. The client calculates the applicable local subnet for the current network connection.
+
+## Understand routing behavior
+
+When **Prefer Local Network** is enabled, routing is evaluated in the following order:
+
+1. Intelligent Local Access, when the configured corporate network detection and application conditions are met.
+1. Home network support for a destination in an eligible directly connected local subnet.
+1. Normal Private Access traffic acquisition and tunneling.
+
+Intelligent Local Access takes precedence so that its authentication requirements can be applied.
+
+### Overlapping corporate and local destinations
+
+A local resource and a corporate private application can use the same IP address or subnet. When **Prefer Local Network** is enabled, a matching destination uses the local path. The corporate resource in the overlapping range isn't reachable through Private Access from that network.
+
+To reach the corporate resource, the user can temporarily turn off **Prefer Local Network**. The client then applies the organization's Private Access forwarding rules.
+
+> [!CAUTION]
+> Enable this capability only for users who need access to local resources. Where possible, avoid configuring corporate applications with address ranges that are likely to overlap users' directly connected home subnets.
+
+## Verify local network routing
+
+Use **Advanced diagnostics** in the Global Secure Access client to verify the routing decision:
+
+1. Open the Global Secure Access client.
+1. Select **Troubleshooting** > **Advanced diagnostics**.
+1. In **Forwarding Profile**, verify that the expected Private Access profile was received.
+1. Open the network traffic view and start collecting traffic.
+1. Connect to the local resource.
+1. Filter the results by the destination IP address.
+1. Verify that the action indicates local bypass.
+
+For more information, see [Global Secure Access client advanced diagnostics](troubleshoot-global-secure-access-client-advanced-diagnostics.md).
+
+## Troubleshoot home network access
+
+### The local resource is still unreachable
+
+- Confirm that **Prefer Local Network** is available and enabled in the client.
+- Confirm that the destination is in the device's directly connected subnet.
+- Confirm that the destination uses an RFC 1918 IPv4 address.
+- In **Advanced diagnostics**, verify that the expected traffic forwarding profile reached the client.
+- Collect traffic while reproducing the issue and review the action for the destination IP address.
+- Verify that the local device and operating-system firewall allow the connection.
+
+### A corporate private application is unreachable
+
+The corporate application's address might overlap the local subnet. Turn off **Prefer Local Network** and try the connection again. If the connection succeeds, the local preference was taking precedence over Private Access for that destination.
+
+Consider publishing the corporate application by FQDN with a more specific application segment or changing the addressing plan to avoid the overlap.
+
+### Prefer Local Network isn't displayed
+
+- Verify that the device runs a supported Global Secure Access client version.
+- Verify that the administrator enabled home network support for the user's Private Access traffic forwarding profile.
+- Verify that the user is assigned to the expected profile.
+- Refresh the client configuration or restart the client after the profile change.
+
+## Limitations
+
+- Home network support applies only to directly connected local subnets. It doesn't provide a general bypass for routed networks behind the local gateway.
+- Only IPv4 private ranges defined by RFC 1918 are supported. IPv6 local subnets aren't supported.
+- Mobile clients aren't supported.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [What is Microsoft Entra Private Access?](concept-private-access.md)
+- [Configure Private Access traffic forwarding](tutorial-private-access-enable-traffic-forwarding.md)
+- [Global Secure Access client overview](concept-clients.md)
+- [Configure Intelligent Local Access](tutorial-private-access-intelligent-local-access.md)
+- [Troubleshoot the Global Secure Access client with Advanced diagnostics](troubleshoot-global-secure-access-client-advanced-diagnostics.md)

diff --git a/docs/id-governance/entitlement-management-sap-ac-integration.md b/docs/id-governance/entitlement-management-sap-ac-integration.md new file mode 100644 index 00000000000..a49220344e6 --- /dev/null +++ b/docs/id-governance/entitlement-management-sap-ac-integration.md @@ -0,0 +1,308 @@ +--- +title: Microsoft Entra SAP Access Control integration (Preview) +description: Learn how to integrate SAP Access Control (SAP AC/GRC) with Microsoft Entra ID Governance so users can request SAP business roles through entitlement management access packages. +author: sponnada +ms.author: sriponnada +manager: teeearls +ms.service: entra-id-governance +ms.subservice: entitlement-management +ms.topic: how-to +ms.date: 09/08/2026 +--- + +# Microsoft Entra SAP Access Control integration (Preview) + +Microsoft Entra ID Governance integrates with SAP Access Control (SAP AC), part of the SAP Governance, Risk and Compliance solution (SAP GRC), so you can govern SAP access from Microsoft Entra. With this integration, you add SAP business roles as resources in entitlement management catalogs and let users request them through Microsoft Entra access packages, while SAP AC continues to run its own approval, risk analysis, and provisioning workflows. + +This integration enables you to: + +- Add SAP AC business roles as resources in entitlement management catalogs. +- Let users request SAP access through Microsoft Entra access packages and the My Access portal. +- Keep SAP AC as the system of record for SAP-side approval and provisioning. +- Reconcile the SAP request outcome back to Microsoft Entra so the assignment status reflects the SAP result. + +Microsoft Entra defines and governs *who can request* access; SAP AC *executes* the request within SAP; and SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP) connects the two in a secure, controlled way. + +> [!IMPORTANT] +> The Microsoft Entra SAP AC integration is currently in PREVIEW. See the [Supplemental Terms of Use for Microsoft Azure Previews](https://azure.microsoft.com/support/legal/preview-supplemental-terms/) for legal terms that apply to Microsoft Entra features that are in beta, preview, or otherwise not yet released into general availability. + +## How the integration works + +The [SAP Identity Access Governance (IAG) integration](entitlement-management-sap-integration.md) and SAP AC integration use different connectivity paths. The SAP IAG integration connects through SAP Cloud Identity Services, while the SAP AC integration reaches your on-premises SAP AC system through SAP BTP. The SAP AC request path is: + +**Microsoft Entra ID Governance entitlement management → SAP BTP Integration Suite (iFlows) → SAP Cloud Connector → on-premises SAP AC** + +- Microsoft Entra never calls SAP AC directly. It calls the OAuth-protected SAP Integration Suite runtime endpoint. +- SAP Integration Suite iFlows translate Microsoft Entra's REST calls into the SOAP web-service calls that SAP AC exposes. +- SAP Cloud Connector provides the secure tunnel from SAP BTP to the on-premises SAP AC system. SAP AC is never exposed directly to the internet. +- SAP AC processes the request using its existing business roles, workflows, approvals, and risk controls. +- Microsoft Entra polls SAP AC for request status through the same chain, and updates the access-package assignment when SAP completes its workflow. Status reconciliation can take up to 10 minutes. + +The following diagram shows the request and status-reconciliation path across Microsoft Entra, SAP BTP, and the on-premises SAP AC system. + +```mermaid +flowchart LR + subgraph MS["Microsoft cloud"] + EM["Microsoft Entra ID Governance
Entitlement management"] + KV["Azure Key Vault
SAP BTP client secret"] + end + subgraph BTP["SAP Business Technology Platform"] + IS["SAP Integration Suite
iFlows: REST to SOAP"] + end + subgraph ONPREM["Customer network (on-premises)"] + CC["SAP Cloud Connector
secure tunnel"] + AC["SAP AC
SAP GRC"] + end + KV -. "connector reads secret" .-> EM + EM -- "1. REST call with OAuth token" --> IS + IS -- "2. SOAP via virtual host" --> CC + CC -- "3. SOAP" --> AC + AC -. "4. request status (polled)" .-> CC + CC -. "status" .-> IS + IS -. "status" .-> EM +``` + + + +## License requirements + +[!INCLUDE [active-directory-p2-governance-license.md](~/includes/entra-p2-governance-license.md)] + +Using this feature requires Microsoft Entra ID Governance or Microsoft Entra Suite licenses. To find the right license for your requirements, see [Microsoft Entra ID Governance licensing fundamentals](licensing-fundamentals.md). + +## Prerequisites + +### SAP prerequisites + +- A working on-premises **SAP AC** system. +- **SAP Cloud Connector** installed in your network and connected to the SAP BTP subaccount you use for this integration. +- An **SAP BTP subaccount** with: + - A subscription to **SAP Integration Suite**. + - The `integrationflows` entitlement and an appropriate quota for creating integration flows. +- Appropriate SAP licensing for **SAP Integration Suite** and **SAP AC**. +- The SAP AC role **`SAP_GRAC_ALL`** assigned to a technical (service) account that is authorized to call the SAP AC SOAP web services. +- An SAP AC user that corresponds to the administrator who creates the connector, holding at least one of these SAP AC authorization roles: `SAP_GRAC_ALL`, `SAP_GRC_FN_ALL`, `ZSAP_GRAC_ALL`, or `ZSAP_GRC_FN_ALL`. Microsoft Entra verifies one of these roles during connector creation (see [Step 6](#step-6-connect-sap-ac-in-microsoft-entra)). + +> [!NOTE] +> The SAP AC system must also be available in SAP AC as a target or managed connector. Run a repository synchronization job for this system to bring its user and user authorization information into SAP AC. + +### Microsoft prerequisites + +- A Microsoft Entra ID Governance license, Microsoft Entra Suite license, or Microsoft Entra ID Governance step-up. +- One of the following administrator roles: [Global Administrator](../identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#global-administrator) or [Identity Governance Administrator](../identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#identity-governance-administrator). +- An **Azure subscription** that contains an **Azure Key Vault** used to store the SAP BTP client secret. + +## Step 1: Prepare SAP AC + +Configure SAP AC to expose and authorize the SOAP web services that the integration calls. + +1. In SAP AC, open transaction **`SICF`** and activate each web service listed in the following table. +1. In SAP SOA Manager, confirm that each service has an active binding and that its alternate-access URL alias exactly matches the value in the table. +1. Test each service endpoint from a system that can reach SAP AC. Resolve any network, authorization, or binding errors before configuring SAP Cloud Connector. +1. Create or identify a technical user or service account, and assign it the `SAP_GRAC_ALL` role so that it can call the SAP AC SOAP web services. + +### Required SAP AC web services and aliases + +The iFlows call SAP AC using fixed alternate-access URL aliases. These alias names are hard-coded in the integration flows and must match **exactly**. Do not rename them in SAP AC or in the iFlows. + +| SAP AC/GRC web service | Required alternate-access URL alias | +| --- | --- | +| `GRAC_LOOKUP_WS` | `/grac_lookup_ws` | +| `GRAC_REQUEST_STATUS_WS` | `/grac_request_status_ws` | +| `GRAC_ROLE_DETAILS_WS` | `/grac_role_details_ws` | +| `GRAC_SEARCH_ROLES_WS` | `/grac_search_roles_ws` | +| `GRAC_SELECT_APPL_WS` | `/grac_select_appl_ws` | +| `GRAC_USER_ACCESS_WS` | `/grac_user_access_ws` | +| `GRAC_USER_EXISTING_ASSGN_WS` | `/grac_user_existing_assgn_ws` | + +> [!NOTE] +> If a SOAP call later returns `404 Not Found`, a mismatched or inactive binding is the most common cause. + +## Step 2: Configure SAP Cloud Connector + +SAP Cloud Connector provides the secure tunnel from your SAP BTP subaccount to the on-premises SAP AC system. + +### Create the system mapping + +1. Open the Cloud Connector administration UI (typically `https://:8443`). +1. Select the subaccount that contains the SAP Integration Suite subscription used for this integration. +1. Go to **Cloud To On-Premises** and add a new system mapping: + + | Setting | Value | + | --- | --- | + | Back-end Type | `ABAP System` | + | Protocol | `HTTPS` (recommended) or `HTTP` | + | Internal Host | Your SAP AC hostname | + | Internal Port | Your SAP AC HTTPS port | + | Virtual Host | A virtual hostname that BTP uses to reach SAP AC | + | Virtual Port | A virtual port that BTP uses to reach SAP AC | + + You enter the same **virtual host** and **virtual port** in each applicable iFlow in the next step. + +### Restrict resource access + +Add resource-access rules for **only** the SOAP service paths required by the integration. + +> [!WARNING] +> Do not expose `/sap/` or create broad access to the entire SAP namespace. Permit only the specific service paths the integration needs. Limiting the exposed paths reduces the attack surface reachable through Cloud Connector. + +### Validate connectivity + +Confirm all of the following: + +- The SAP AC system mapping shows **Reachable** in Cloud Connector. +- The subaccount connection is active. +- In SAP BTP Cockpit, under **Connectivity** > **Cloud Connectors**, the Cloud Connector shows **Connected**. +- After you import the iFlows, a test call from BTP resolves through the configured virtual host. + +## Step 3: Set up SAP BTP Integration Suite + +For the preview, the integration is distributed as a downloadable ZIP package of integration flows. + +### Import the integration package + +1. Download the integration-flow ZIP package from the preview team's GitHub repository (``). +1. Sign in to your SAP BTP subaccount and open **SAP Integration Suite** > **Design** > **Integrations**. +1. Select **Import** and upload the ZIP file. +1. Confirm that the imported package and all of its integration flows are listed. The package contains one flow for each SAP AC web service the integration uses. + +### Configure each iFlow + +Modify only the parameters called out here. Don't change the preconfigured alias names or endpoint paths. + +For each applicable iFlow, set: + +- **Destination / virtual host** — the exact virtual host and port you created in Cloud Connector (`:`). +- **Authentication to SAP AC** — the credentials for the SAP AC technical user (the account that holds `SAP_GRAC_ALL`). + +### Deploy the iFlows + +1. Save each flow's configuration and select **Deploy**. +1. Monitor deployment and confirm every flow reaches **Started** status. +1. Record the runtime endpoint URLs; they follow the pattern `https://.it-.cfapps..hana.ondemand.com/...`. + +## Step 4: Get the SAP BTP authentication credentials + +Microsoft Entra authenticates to the SAP Integration Suite endpoint using the **OAuth 2.0 client-credentials** flow. The credentials come from a service key on the SAP BTP Integration Suite runtime (service **SAP Process Integration Runtime**, plan **integration-flow**, service technical name `it-rt`). + +Create or open the service key and record these values: + +| Field | Description | +| --- | --- | +| `clientid` | OAuth client ID for the Integration Suite runtime | +| `clientsecret` | OAuth client secret | +| `tokenurl` | OAuth token endpoint base URL | +| `url` | Integration Suite runtime base URL | + +You use these values when you create the Microsoft Entra connector in Step 6. + +## Step 5: Configure Azure Key Vault + +Microsoft Entra reads the SAP BTP client secret from an Azure Key Vault rather than storing it in the connector. + +1. [Create an Azure Key Vault](/azure/key-vault/general/quick-create-portal) (or use an existing one) in your Azure subscription. +1. Under **Settings** > **Networking**, select **Allow public access from all networks**. + + > [!NOTE] + > The preview connector requires public network access on the Key Vault. Private endpoints and selected-network configurations aren't supported for the preview. + +1. [Add a secret](/azure/key-vault/secrets/quick-create-portal) whose value is the `clientsecret` from your SAP BTP service key. Record the **subscription**, **Key Vault name**, and **secret name**. + +### Assign Key Vault permissions + +During connector creation, the signed-in administrator needs access to the Key Vault to select and validate the secret. After the connector is created, the Microsoft Entra ID Governance service principal runs the integration as a background service. It reads the SAP BTP client secret from Key Vault each time it submits a request or polls SAP AC for status. Therefore, both the administrator who configures the connector and the service principal need access to the Key Vault. + +- The user performing setup needs the **Owner** and **Key Vault Secrets Officer** roles on the Key Vault. +- The following service principal is added automatically as part of connector configuration. Assign it the **Key Vault Secrets User** role on the Key Vault after it appears in your tenant: + + | Service principal | Application ID | + | --- | --- | + | Microsoft Entra ID Governance - SAP Cloud Identity Access Governance | `22223333-cccc-4444-dddd-5555eeee6666` | + +## Step 6: Connect SAP AC in Microsoft Entra + +When you create the connector, Microsoft Entra calls the `GRAC_USER_EXISTING_ASSGN_WS` web service to read the SAP AC roles assigned to the SAP AC user that corresponds to the administrator creating the connector. Creation succeeds only if that user holds at least one of these SAP AC authorization roles: + +- `SAP_GRAC_ALL` +- `SAP_GRC_FN_ALL` +- `ZSAP_GRAC_ALL` +- `ZSAP_GRC_FN_ALL` + +If none of these roles is assigned, connector creation fails with a *not authorized* error. + +1. In the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com), browse to **ID Governance** > **Entitlement management** > **Control configurations**. +1. On the **Manage External Connectors (Preview)** card, select **View Connectors**. +1. Select **+ New connector**, and in **Type** select **SAP AC**. +1. Complete the connector fields: + + | Field | What to enter | + | --- | --- | + | Type | `SAP AC` | + | Name | A custom name for the connector | + | Description | A description for the connector | + | Subscription ID | The Azure subscription that contains your Key Vault | + | Key Vault Name | The Key Vault that stores the SAP BTP client secret | + | Secret Name | The Key Vault secret containing the SAP BTP `clientsecret` | + | Client ID | The `clientid` from your SAP BTP service key | + | Access Token URL | The `tokenurl` from your SAP BTP service key, with `/oauth/token` appended. Example: `https://.authentication..hana.ondemand.com/oauth/token` | + | AC URL | The `url` from your SAP BTP service key, with `/http/` appended. Example: `https://.it-.cfapps..hana.ondemand.com/http/` | + | System ID | The system ID of your on-premises SAP AC instance. Example: `AC1` | + | User Identifier | The Microsoft Entra attribute that maps to the user's SAP AC/GRC username. Example: `userPrincipalName` | + + > [!IMPORTANT] + > The **AC URL** is the SAP Integration Suite runtime URL — not the SAP AC host URL — and must end with `/http/`. Don't paste the client secret into any field; the connector reads it from Key Vault. + +1. Select **Create**. + +Catalog administrators can now add SAP AC business roles to entitlement management catalogs and access packages. + +## Step 7: Add SAP business roles to a catalog + +1. In the Microsoft Entra admin center, browse to **ID Governance** > **Entitlement management** > **Catalogs**. +1. [Create a new catalog](entitlement-management-catalog-create.md) or open an existing one. +1. On the catalog's **Resources** tab, select **+ Add resource** > **External Resources**. +1. Select the **SAP AC** connector you configured, then select the SAP AC Access Rights to add. +1. Save the resource selection. + +## Step 8: Create an access package with SAP business roles + +1. In the catalog, open the **Access packages** tab and select **New access package**. Enter the [basic information](entitlement-management-access-package-create.md#configure-basics). +1. On the **Resource roles** tab, select **SAP AC** and choose the business roles to include. +1. On the **Requests** tab, configure who can request the package and the request policy. For end-to-end testing, configure the policy so that **Microsoft Entra approval isn't required** (SAP AC is the approval authority). +1. Complete the remaining tabs and select **Create**. For more information, see [Create an access package in entitlement management](entitlement-management-access-package-create.md). + +## Test the integration + +1. As an Identity Governance Administrator, [directly assign a test user](entitlement-management-access-package-assignments.md#directly-assign-an-identity) to the access package, or have the user [request it](entitlement-management-request-access.md) from the My Access portal. +1. Confirm that the request appears in SAP AC. +1. Approve (or deny) the request in SAP AC. The preview demonstrates a two-level approval in SAP AC. +1. If approved, verify that the role is provisioned in SAP AC and that the assignment status in Microsoft Entra updates to **Delivered**. +1. Allow up to 10 minutes for status to reconcile between the two systems. + +## Troubleshooting + +| Symptom | Checks | +| --- | --- | +| BTP-to-SAP AC connection timeout | Cloud Connector shows **Connected** in SAP BTP Cockpit; the iFlow virtual host and port match the Cloud Connector mapping exactly; resource-access rules permit the required SOAP paths; SAP AC internal host and port are reachable from Cloud Connector. | +| SOAP call returns `403 Forbidden` | The technical user has the required authorizations; the services are activated in `SICF`; the alternate-access URLs match the hard-coded aliases; the SOA bindings are active and correctly named. | +| iFlow deployment fails | The subaccount has the SAP Integration Suite entitlement and quota; the administrator has the required Integration Suite roles (for example, `PIIntegrationDeveloper`); every flow reaches **Started** rather than only saved. | +| Connector can't reach the iFlow endpoint | The runtime endpoint URL is correct; **AC URL** was built from the BTP `url` with `/http/` appended; **Client ID** is correct; the Key Vault secret holds the correct BTP `clientsecret`; **Access Token URL** matches the BTP `tokenurl` (with `/oauth/token`); no firewall blocks outbound traffic from Microsoft Entra to SAP BTP. | +| Connector can't find the Key Vault secret | The subscription, Key Vault, and secret name are correct; you have **Owner** and **Key Vault Secrets Officer**; the required service principal exists and has **Key Vault Secrets User**; Key Vault networking allows public access from all networks. | +| Connector creation fails with a *not authorized* error | The SAP AC user that corresponds to the signed-in administrator holds one of `SAP_GRAC_ALL`, `SAP_GRC_FN_ALL`, `ZSAP_GRAC_ALL`, or `ZSAP_GRC_FN_ALL`; the `GRAC_USER_EXISTING_ASSGN_WS` service is activated and reachable so Microsoft Entra can read the user's existing role assignments; the **User Identifier** attribute maps to the correct SAP AC username. | +| SAP SOAP endpoint returns `404 Not Found` | Verify the endpoint URL, `SICF` activation, the SAP SOA Manager binding, and that the binding names match the names the iFlow expects. | + +## Preview considerations and limitations + +- The integration is in public preview. The iFlow package is distributed as a ZIP from the preview GitHub repository and isn't yet a generally available SAP Integration Suite marketplace package. +- Service aliases are hard-coded and can't be renamed. Modify only the documented iFlow parameters. +- Azure Key Vault must allow public network access for this preview. +- Status reconciliation is polling-based and can take up to 10 minutes; event-driven callback isn't yet available. +- The preview uses the broad SAP role `SAP_GRAC_ALL`; a validated least-privilege role isn't yet defined. If you don't want the integration to use the standard `SAP_GRAC_ALL` role, you can define a custom SAP AC role that grants only the authorizations needed to call the AC SOAP web services. +- Cross-system separation-of-duties analysis, access drift reconciliation, and SAP-scoped administrative delegation aren't yet available. + +## Next steps + +- [Create an access package in entitlement management](entitlement-management-access-package-create.md) +- [Request access to an access package](entitlement-management-request-access.md) +- [Microsoft Entra SAP IAG integration (Preview)](entitlement-management-sap-integration.md)

 1. Confirm that PIM enforces the decision returned by your custom extension:
-   - **Approved**: The activation proceeds through the normal PIM workflow, including any other approval steps.
-   - **AutoApproved**: The activation proceeds without requiring manual PIM approval.

+## Preapproval and postapproval extensions
+
+Preapproval and postapproval extensions are blocking gates, but they run at different points in the activation workflow.
+
+| Capability | `preApproval` | `postApproval` |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Execution point | Before manual approval | After manual approval and immediately before assignment provisioning |
+| Supported outcomes | `Approved`, `Denied`, `AutoApproved` | `approved`, `denied`, `deferred` |
+| Skip manual approval | Yes, with `AutoApproved` | No, because manual approval is already complete |
+| Deferred evaluation | No | Yes, through `/updateRequest` |
+| Blocks | Manual approval and provisioning | Assignment provisioning |
+| Common scenarios | Compliance prescreening, risk assessment, early denial, and conditional automatic approval | IT service management validation, security scanning, external approval, and asynchronous processing |
+
+Use a preapproval extension to evaluate a request before a PIM approver sees it. Use a postapproval extension when custom logic must run after the built-in PIM approval stage but before PIM provisions the assignment.
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> A postapproval extension doesn't run after role activation. It runs after manual approval, but before the role assignment is provisioned.
+
+### When to use each extension type
+
+Use a preapproval extension to:
+
+- Perform compliance or risk checks before a human approver sees the request.
+- Auto-approve low-risk requests that meet defined criteria.
+- Deny requests early based on external data.
+- Reduce approver workload by filtering clearly valid or invalid requests.
+
+Use a postapproval extension to:
+
+- Run another custom approval workflow after PIM approval.
+- Validate an IT service management ticket before provisioning access.
+- Perform a security scan or another long-running process.
+- Defer the decision and call PIM later with the final outcome.
+
+### Complete a deferred postapproval evaluation
+
+A postapproval extension can return `deferred` when it needs more time to make a decision. PIM places the request in `PostApprovalExtensionPendingEvaluation` and doesn't provision the role assignment. After the asynchronous process finishes, the extension calls `/updateRequest` on the original activation request with a final `approved` or `denied` decision.
+
+The extension must authenticate to the callback API by using the same Microsoft Entra app registration configured for the extension. PIM verifies that the calling application ID matches the registered application. The callback can't return `deferred` again.
+
+The deferred flow works as follows:
+
+1. PIM calls the postapproval extension after manual approval.
+1. The extension returns `deferred` because it needs more time.
+1. PIM moves the request to `PostApprovalExtensionPendingEvaluation`.
+1. The extension completes its asynchronous validation or approval process.
+1. The extension calls the provider-specific `/updateRequest` endpoint with `approved` or `denied`.
+1. PIM validates the callback and either provisions or denies the assignment.
+
+#### Microsoft Entra roles
+
+Use:
+
+```http
+POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignmentScheduleRequests/{requestId}/updateRequest
+Content-Type: application/json
+```
+
+```json
+{
+  "evaluationOutcome": "approved",
+  "evaluationId": "aaaa0000-bb11-2222-33cc-444444dddddd",
+  "reason": "The external compliance system approved the request."
+}
+```
+
+#### PIM for Groups
+
+Use:
+
+```http
+POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/identityGovernance/privilegedAccess/group/assignmentScheduleRequests/{requestId}/updateRequest
+Content-Type: application/json
+```
+
+```json
+{
+  "evaluationOutcome": "denied",
+  "evaluationId": "aaaa0000-bb11-2222-33cc-444444dddddd",
+  "reason": "The external compliance system denied the request."
+}
+```
+
+#### Azure resources
+
+Use:
+
+```http
+POST https://management.azure.com/{scope}/providers/Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignmentScheduleRequests/{requestId}/updateRequest?api-version=2020-10-01
+Content-Type: application/json
+```
+
+```json
+{
+  "evaluationOutcome": "denied",
+  "evaluationId": "aaaa0000-bb11-2222-33cc-444444dddddd",
+  "reason": [
+    "The change advisory board rejected ticket CHANGE-9921."
+  ]
+}
+```
+
+#### Callback endpoint summary
+
+| Provider | Endpoint |
+|---|---|
+| Microsoft Entra roles | `POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignmentScheduleRequests/{requestId}/updateRequest` |
+| PIM for Groups | `POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/identityGovernance/privilegedAccess/group/assignmentScheduleRequests/{requestId}/updateRequest` |
+| Azure resources | `POST https://management.azure.com/{scope}/providers/Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignmentScheduleRequests/{requestId}/updateRequest?api-version=2020-10-01` |
+
+The callback request body supports the following properties:
+
+| Property | Required | Description |
+|---|---|---|
+| `evaluationOutcome` | Yes | Final outcome. Use `approved` or `denied`; a callback can't return `deferred`. |
+| `evaluationId` | Yes | Correlation identifier from the original extension response. |
+| `reason` | No | Human-readable reason for the decision. Azure Resource Manager accepts a string collection; Microsoft Graph accepts a string. |
+| `scheduleInfo` | No | Microsoft Graph only. Optional updated activation schedule for an approved request. |
+
+Handle callback failures based on the returned HTTP status:
+
+| HTTP status | Cause |
+|---|---|
+| `400 Bad Request` | The request isn't waiting for a callback, or the callback outcome isn't `approved` or `denied`. |
+| `401 Unauthorized` | The calling application doesn't match the app registered for the custom extension. |
+| `404 Not Found` | The request ID doesn't exist. |
+
+## Custom attributes
+
+Custom attributes collect extra key-value context during activation and include it in the extension request. Use custom attributes when your extension needs information that isn't part of the standard request, such as a cost center, project code, business justification category, or identifier in an external system.
+
+Add the attribute names when you create the extension. During activation, the user enters the corresponding values. PIM sends the values in a provider-specific format.
+
+### Azure resources
+
+For Azure resource roles, PIM sends a `customAttributes` array:
+
+```json
+{
+  "customAttributes": [
+    {
+      "attributeName": "costCenter",
+      "attributeValue": "CC-4521"
+    },
+    {
+      "attributeName": "projectCode",
+      "attributeValue": "PROJ-ALPHA"
+    }
+  ]
+}
+```
+
+### Microsoft Entra roles
+
+For Microsoft Entra roles, PIM sends a JSON-encoded `customData` string:
+
+```json
+{
+  "customData": "{\"costCenter\":\"CC-4521\",\"projectCode\":\"PROJ-ALPHA\"}"
+}
+```
+
+### PIM for Groups
+
+For PIM for Groups, PIM also sends a JSON-encoded `customData` string:
+
+```json
+{
+  "customData": "{\"costCenter\":\"CC-4521\",\"approverGroup\":\"finance-approvers\"}"
+}
+```
+
+| Provider | Field | Format |
+|---|---|---|
+| Azure resources | `customAttributes` | Array of `attributeName` and `attributeValue` objects. |
+| Microsoft Entra roles | `customData` | JSON-encoded string. |
+| PIM for Groups | `customData` | JSON-encoded string. |
+
+Validate custom-attribute names and values in your API before using them in a query, workflow, or access decision.
+
+## Quick reference
+
+### Extension type decision matrix
+
+| Scenario | `preApproval` | `postApproval` |
+|---|---|---|
+| Compliance check before approvers | Best fit | Not applicable |
+| Auto-approve low-risk requests | Best fit | Not supported |
+| Block based on external data | Supported | Supported |
+| Custom approval after PIM approval | Not applicable | Best fit |
+| Asynchronous processing with callback | Not supported | Best fit |
+| Security scan before provisioning | Not applicable | Best fit |
+
+### Evaluation outcome quick reference
+
+| Outcome | `preApproval` effect | `postApproval` effect | Callback effect |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| `Approved` / `approved` | Continues to manual approval. | Continues to provisioning. | Resolves a deferred request and provisions the role. |
+| `Denied` / `denied` | Denies the request. | Denies the request. | Resolves a deferred request and denies it. |
+| `deferred` | Not supported. | Pauses and waits for `/updateRequest`. | Not supported; a callback can't defer again. |
+| `AutoApproved` | Skips manual approval. | Not supported. | Not supported. |
+
+### Postapproval request status transitions
+
+The following table shows how the request status transitions based on the postapproval evaluation outcome and the callback decision:
+
+| Stage | Outcome | New status | Next step |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| Postapproval extension | `approved` | Granted | PIM provisions the assignment. |
+| Postapproval extension | `denied` | Denied | The request ends. |
+| Postapproval extension | `deferred` | `PostApprovalExtensionPendingEvaluation` | PIM waits for `/updateRequest`. |
+| Callback | `approved` | `PostApprovalExtensionAdminApproved` | PIM provisions the assignment. |
+| Callback | `denied` | `PostApprovalExtensionAdminDenied` | The request ends. |

+## Manage individual Security Defaults protections (preview)
+
+Organizations need to protect their accounts from common identity attacks, even when they don't have the resources to build and maintain custom security policies. Security Defaults provides a Microsoft-managed security baseline that helps protect accounts with multifactor authentication (MFA) and blocks vulnerable or commonly abused sign-in methods.
+
+The original Security Defaults experience uses one on/off setting for all protections. The updated experience introduces individual rules, so administrators can see what each protection does, whom it covers, and whether it's enabled. You can change one protection without turning off the others.
+
+This article explains how to manage these protections in **Microsoft Entra ID Free**. Security Defaults is available at no extra cost; no P1 or P2 license is required for the baseline protections.
+
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> The updated experience is in private preview for selected Microsoft Entra ID Free tenants. Available protections can vary during the preview.
+
+### Why use Security Defaults?
+
+- **Start with a Microsoft-managed baseline.** Use preconfigured protections without creating and maintaining your own policies.
+- **Understand your settings.** Review the purpose, scope, and state of each protection.
+- **Manage protections individually.** Change a specific protection while leaving the other rules in place.
+
+### Relationship to Conditional Access
+
+The updated Security Defaults baseline can work alongside customer-created Conditional Access policies. Unlike the original experience, it doesn't require you to disable Security Defaults to use Conditional Access.
+
+Security Defaults provides the common baseline across free and premium tenants. In the updated model, the management location is:
+
+- **Microsoft Entra ID Free:** Manage individual protections on the **Security Defaults** page, using the steps in this article.
+- **Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2:** Manage the same baseline as a Microsoft-managed **Security Defaults policy plan** in **Conditional Access**.
+
+Organizations can use custom Conditional Access policies for additional requirements, such as device compliance or location-based controls. Creating those policies requires the appropriate premium license.
+
+At sign-in, every applicable Security Defaults rule and Conditional Access policy must be satisfied. The baseline and custom policies work together; one doesn't replace the other.
+
+### Security Defaults protections
+
+The updated experience brings together four Microsoft-managed rules. Each rule defines the sign-ins it covers and the protection it applies. Microsoft manages the rule definitions, while administrators control whether each rule is enabled.
+
+#### Require MFA for administrators
+
+Administrator accounts can change settings, manage users, and access sensitive resources. Requiring MFA helps protect those accounts if a password is stolen.
+
+This rule requires MFA for administrator sign-ins that match its scope. Open the rule to see the administrator roles and resources it covers.
+
+#### Require MFA for all users
+
+Ordinary user accounts also need protection. An attacker who gains access to a user account can read information or use that account to target other people in the organization.
+
+This rule requires MFA for all users within its scope, including administrators. It broadens the original Security Defaults behavior from requiring MFA **when necessary** to requiring MFA for the sign-ins covered by the rule.
+
+Users who haven't registered an authentication method might be asked to do so during sign-in. A valid existing MFA sign-in can satisfy the requirement, so users won't necessarily receive a new MFA prompt every time.
+
+#### Block legacy authentication
+
+Legacy authentication refers to older sign-in methods that don't support MFA, such as basic authentication used by older mail clients and applications.
+
+When enabled, this rule blocks sign-ins that use legacy authentication. Applications and devices that depend on those methods need to use modern authentication to continue signing in.
+
+#### Block device code flow
+
+Device code flow lets an application or device ask the user to complete sign-in in a separate browser. It's useful for devices with limited input capabilities, but attackers can abuse it by tricking users into entering a code that gives the attacker access.
+
+When enabled, this rule blocks sign-ins that use device code flow. Applications and devices that rely on this flow need an alternative sign-in method.
+
+### Required roles
+
+To view and change Security Defaults protections, use one of the following Microsoft Entra roles:
+
+- **Conditional Access Administrator**
+- **Security Administrator**
+- **Global Administrator**
+
+**Global Reader** and **Security Reader** can view the protections but can't change them.
+
+Use the least-privileged role needed for the task. Conditional Access Administrator is recommended for managing these settings.
+
+### Manage a protection
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) with one of the roles that can change protections.
+2. Switch to the free tenant enabled for your private preview.
+3. Open the access link provided in your preview invitation.
+4. On the **Security Defaults** page, select the name of a protection.
+5. Review its description, current state, and the users, roles, or resources it covers.
+6. Turn the protection on or off and follow the confirmation prompt. If you're turning it off, provide the requested feedback.
+7. Confirm that the updated state is shown on the page.
+
+The change applies to the tenant, not just the administrator making it. Each rule is managed independently. For example, turning off the administrator MFA rule can still leave administrators covered by the all-users MFA rule.
+
+Microsoft recommends keeping protections enabled. Turning off a protection reduces security for the sign-ins it covers.
+
+### Prepare your organization
+
+Before enabling or changing protections:
+
+- **Prepare users for MFA.** Make sure administrators and users can complete registration and authentication. Users can review their registered methods through [My Account](https://myprofile.microsoft.com).
+- **Review application compatibility.** Identify applications or devices that rely on legacy authentication or device code flow and plan an alternative sign-in method.
+- **Inform your support team.** Explain the MFA change and how to help users who have trouble registering or signing in.
+
+### Moving to the updated experience
+
+Microsoft introduces the updated controls through a phased rollout. When your tenant receives the update, you manage the Microsoft-provided rules individually instead of using the original single setting. You don't need to recreate the rules.
+
+Rollout communications explain changes to your tenant's protections, including any planned device code flow enablement. Review each rule's state when the update arrives and prepare users for the broader all-users MFA requirement.
+
 ## Next steps
 
 - [Blog: Introducing security defaults](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/t5/azure-active-directory-identity/introducing-security-defaults/ba-p/1061414)

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Entra: Windows Hello for Business and macOS Platform SSO as standalone MFA factors
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Entra will recognize Windows Hello for Business and macOS Platform SSO as standalone MFA factors starting early October 2026, allowing users to meet MFA requirements without additional passkeys. No configuration changes are needed, but organizations should update onboarding and MFA registration guidance accordingly.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated October 13, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

What and why

Microsoft Entra will soon recognize Windows Hello for Business (WHfB) and macOS Platform Single Sign-On (PSSO) as standalone multifactor authentication (MFA) factors in supported authentication scenarios.

Today, WHfB and macOS PSSO can satisfy MFA requirements during primary sign-in, but users may still be required to register and use an additional passkey or authentication method for certain step-up authentication prompts, Authentication Strength policies, and sign-in frequency checks.

After this rollout, users who authenticate with WHfB or macOS PSSO will be able to satisfy supported MFA requirements without registering an additional passkey. This change helps organizations expand the use of phishing-resistant authentication methods and reduce reliance on less secure authentication methods. As part of this change, a user's WHfB and macOS PSSO credentials will be displayed in My Security Info as auto-registered passkeys.

Rollout schedule

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC): Beginning in early October 2026 and expected to complete in mid-December 2026 (previously late November)

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Microsoft Entra ID
  • Users who authenticate with Windows Hello for Business
  • Users who authenticate with macOS Platform SSO
  • Organizations using Conditional Access Authentication Strength policies

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Entra ID
  • Windows Hello for Business
  • macOS Platform SSO
  • Conditional Access
  • Authentication Strength policies

What will happen

After rollout:

  • Users signing in with WHfB or macOS PSSO can complete supported MFA challenges without requiring a separate passkey.
  • WHfB and macOS PSSO will satisfy supported MFA requirements for step-up authentication scenarios.
  • WHfB and macOS PSSO can be used during 2FA to satisfy supported Authentication Strength policy requirements.
  • WHfB and macOS PSSO can be used during 2FA to satisfy supported sign-in frequency challenge requirements.
  • Users whose only MFA method is WHfB or macOS PSSO will be considered MFA-capable.
  • Users who sign in with only a password will no longer be automatically prompted to register an additional MFA method if WHfB or macOS PSSO is their only registered MFA credential.
  • Users with WHfB or macOS PSSO credentials, will be able to see them listed in My Security Info as auto-registered passkeys.

Action required and recommendations

No configuration changes are required.

We recommend reviewing user onboarding and MFA registration processes before rollout. Because WHfB and macOS PSSO credentials are device-bound, users may not be able to complete MFA challenges from devices where those credentials are not available.

Recommended actions:

  • Update onboarding guidance to ensure users register at least one portable MFA method.
  • Consider requiring users to register a synced passkey or Microsoft Authenticator passkey in addition to WHfB or macOS PSSO.
  • Review custom Authentication Strength policies to confirm WHfB and macOS PSSO are allowed where appropriate.
  • Update user documentation because users with only WHfB or macOS PSSO registered will no longer be automatically guided to register an additional MFA method.

Learn more (To be updated closer to GA rollout.)

  • Plan a Windows Hello for Business deployment | Security | Windows | Microsoft Learn
  • Prepare users to provision and use Windows Hello for Business | Security | Windows | Microsoft Learn

Compliance considerations

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

messageCenterItems.title: Action may be required: Review who can create agents in Microsoft Entra
messageCenterItems.summary: Starting November 4, 2026, default users in Microsoft Entra can create agent blueprints unless administrators disable this via the "Users can create agent blueprints" setting. Admins can restrict this by toggling the setting to No in the Entra admin center before rollout completes in late November.
messageCenterItems.body:
What and why

Microsoft Entra is changing who can create agent blueprints by default. Starting November 4, default users will be able to create new agent blueprints unless an administrator turns off Users can create agent blueprints. This means that users without built-in or custom Entra roles will be able to create new agent blueprints in their organization. From now until rollout begins, you can set your tenant preferences to prepare for this rollout. If you do not want users in your organization to create new agent blueprints and their identities, follow the instructions below. 

Rollout schedule

  • Worldwide: Beginning in early November 2026 and expected to complete by late November 2026

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Microsoft Entra
  • Default users who don't have a built-in or custom Microsoft Entra role

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Entra

What will happen

  • Default users will be able to create agent blueprints unless an administrator turns off Users can create agent blueprints. If you set the toggle to No, default users will not be able to create new agents. Supported administrators and users assigned the Agent ID Developer role can continue to create them. 
  • If you change this toggle now, your tenant won't change right away. Your setting takes effect when the rollout begins in early November.

Action required and recommendations

If default users should be allowed to create agents in your organization, no action is required. Choosing to allow users to create agent blueprints will not begin until the functionality is available in your tenant.

To restrict creation:

  1. Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center using this link.
  2. Go to Entra ID > Users > User settings.
  3. Under Default user role permissions, find Users can create agent blueprints.
  4. Set the toggle to No, then save the change.

For more information and instructions on setting the toggle for your organization, see Manage who can create agent blueprints here.

This change affects new agent blueprint creation by default users. It does not:

  • Change or remove existing agent blueprints.
  • Change who can create agent identities from existing blueprints.
  • Block an app or an agent from creating identities
  • Affect creation requirements within platforms such as Microsoft Foundry or Security Copilot, such as requiring licenses and Azure subscriptions.

The new setting is independent of Users can register applications. Review both settings separately.

Learn more

  • Delegate application management administrator permissions - Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Learn

Compliance considerations

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Entra: Changes to AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager permission for agent identities
messageCenterItems.summary: Starting November 4, Microsoft Entra will stop automatically granting the AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager permission to agent blueprints. Admin consent will be required for agents to create identities. This change, rolling out worldwide in November 2026, enhances control and auditability of agent identity creation.
messageCenterItems.body:
What and why

Microsoft Entra Agent ID is enforcing tighter restrictions for autonomous creation of an agent’s own identities. Currently, all agents are granted AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager upon creation without administrator approval. Starting November 4, Microsoft Entra will no longer automatically grant AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager to agent blueprint principals, and creation of identities will need an admin to grant consent.

Agents that use app-only authentication to create their own agent identities must be explicitly granted the AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager Microsoft Graph application permission or move to another supported authorization model before enforcement reaches their tenant.

Rollout schedule

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in early November 2026 and expected to complete by late November 2026

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Microsoft Entra 
  • No action is required if your organization doesn't have an agent that depends on the automatic AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager grant.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Entra

What will happen

Today, an agent blueprint principal is granted AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager automatically. This implicit grant allows the principal to create agent identities without a tenant-admin granting an app-role assignment.

After enforcement, an administrator must grant the Microsoft Graph application permission AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager to agents that needs this authority.

This change:

  • Makes app-only agent identity creation authority visible, auditable, and revocable.
  • Makes AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager revocable if consented
  • Affects existing and future agents.
  • Doesn't remove existing agent identities or agent blueprints.
  • Doesn't remove the ability for agent identity blueprints to create agent identities, when AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager is explicitly granted by an administrator
  • Doesn't affect an agent that uses a directory role to authorize creation of agent identities.

Action required and recommendations

No action is required if your organization doesn't have an agent that depends on the automatic AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager grant.

Identify agents that create agent identities without a signed-in user.

  1. Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center.
  2. Go to Entra ID>Audit Logs.
  3. Set the Category to "ApplicationManagement"
  4. Set the Activity filter to "Add Service Principal"

Find events where the Initiated By (actor) Type is Application and the Target is an agent identity.

For each affected agent:

  1. Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center.
  2. Go to Entra ID>Agent blueprints>Search for your agent blueprint>Granted permissions
  3. Review if the Agent has any other granted permissions that may allow for creation of agent identities. If there are no other permissions allowing for creation, this agent relies on AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager.
  4. Starting October 16, you may grant the explicit AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager Microsoft Graph application permission through tenant-wide admin consent or manual app-role creation. Granting it earlier will cause an error. A successful grant appears in the Granted Permissions table with “An administrator” in the Granted By column.
  5. Test app-only agent identity creation before enforcement begins.
  6. Update operational guidance for a failed request after enforcement.

If an app-only request relies only on the automatic grant after enforcement reaches your tenant, the request will fail with a 403 authorization error.

Learn more

  • For more about how to grant your agents access to resources, visit Grant agents access to Microsoft 365 resources | Microsoft Learn. 
  • For the Microsoft Graph permission reference on AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager, visit Microsoft Graph permissions reference - Microsoft Graph | Microsoft Learn.

Compliance considerations

No specific compliance impacts have been identified for this configuration update.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Entra: Allow password change after secure sign-in with My Sign-Ins
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Entra will enable users to change passwords after secure sign-in using strong credentials (passkey, FIDO2, Windows Hello) without knowing the current password or using SSPR. This feature, disabled by default, requires admin activation and will roll out globally from October to November 2026.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated October 9, 2026: We have updated the content. Thank you for your patience. 

What and Why

We're introducing a new Microsoft Entra capability that allows password change after secure sign-in directly from My Sign-Ins using an existing strong credential, such as a passkey, FIDO2 security key, or Windows Hello for Business. Users can complete this action even if they don't know their current password and without using self-service password reset (SSPR) or contacting the helpdesk.

Many organizations are adopting allowed password changes after secure sign-ins but still maintain passwords for legacy applications and services. This update helps reduce password-related support requests and removes a common barrier to adoption. The feature is disabled by default and requires administrator enablement before users can access it.

Rollout Schedule

  • General Availability (Worldwide and GCC): Beginning end of October 2026 (previously mid-October) and expected to complete by end of November 2026 (previously late October)

Impact on Your Organization

Who is affected

  • Microsoft Entra administrators who manage password change settings
  • Users who have a registered allowed password change after secure sign-in method (passkey, FIDO2 security key, or Windows Hello for Business) and also maintain a password
  • Organizations that choose to enable the feature

Platforms/Services

  • Microsoft Entra
  • My Sign-Ins (mysignins.microsoft.com)

What will happen

  • Because this feature is off by default, there is no change to your users' experience unless you turn it on. 
  • After the feature is enabled, eligible users will see a new Change password option in My Sign-Ins.
  • Users can authenticate set a new password without knowing their existing password.
  • Users are not required to enroll in or use SSPR to complete this action.
  • Administrators can choose to enable or disable the capability through Microsoft Entra management interfaces available at release.
  • Authentication continues to require a strong password change method, such as a passkey, FIDO2 security key, or Windows Hello for Business.
  • The setting is tenant-wide: you can turn it on for your entire tenant or leave it off for everyone. There is no per-user or per-group scoping. 

Action Required/Recommendations

No action is required.

If your organization plans to support allowed password changes after secure sign-in:

  • Review your password management and allowed password changes after secure sign-in strategy.
  • Evaluate whether enabling this capability aligns with your organization's security and support requirements.
  • Communicate the new self-service capability to helpdesk and support teams.
  • Update internal user guidance and documentation as needed.
  • If your organization chooses to offer allowed password changes after secure sign-in, enable the feature through the Microsoft Entra admin experience or supported APIs when it becomes available in October 2026.

Learn more 

  • Microsoft Learn documentation will be available when the feature releases in October. 

Compliance Considerations

QuestionAnswer
Does the change include an admin control?Yes. The feature is disabled by default and requires explicit administrator enablement.
Does the change modify how users can access or correct their personal data?Yes. Users gain a new self-service method to update their password using an existing allowed password change after secure sign-in.

messageCenterItems.title: Reminder: Microsoft‑managed CA policy will be enforced soon — Require risk remediation for high‑risk users
messageCenterItems.summary: To strengthen your organization's security posture, Microsoft created a new Microsoft‑managed Conditional Access (CA) policy—Require risk remediation for high‑risk users—in your tenant, along with a new security group for this policy.  This policy uses Microsoft Entra ID Protection to identify users at high risk and prompts them to self‑remediate through adaptive risk remediation, allowing users to resolve their own risk without administrator intervention.
messageCenterItems.body:
To strengthen your organization's security posture, Microsoft created a new Microsoft‑managed Conditional Access (CA) policy—Require risk remediation for high‑risk users—in your tenant, along with a new security group for this policy. This policy uses Microsoft Entra ID Protection to identify users at high risk and prompts them to self‑remediate through adaptive risk remediation, allowing users to resolve their own risk without administrator intervention.

The policy is currently in report‑only mode and the 30‑day evaluation period is ending soon. If you take no action, the policy will automatically switch to On.

When this will happen

The Microsoft‑managed CA policy was created in report‑only mode.

The week of October 28, 2026: End of evaluation period — policy will be enforced (automatically switched to On)

How this affects your organization

Who is affected

  • Organizations with Microsoft Entra ID P2 licenses.

What will happen

  • A new Microsoft‑managed Require risk remediation for high‑risk users CA policy is currently in report‑only mode.
  • If you do not set the policy to On or Off within the remaining evaluation period, it will automatically turn On.
  • When On, users identified as High User Risk will be prompted to self‑remediate. After successful remediation, risk is cleared and access is restored.
  • No existing Conditional Access settings or exclusions (such as break‑glass accounts) will be altered.
  • The policy will remain enabled by default unless customized.

What you can do to prepare

  • Review the policy in the Microsoft Entra admin portal.
  • Decide whether to:
    • Allow the policy to automatically turn on at the end of the evaluation period, or
    • Set it to Off if you do not want the policy enforced.
  • Customize the policy as needed (for example, exclude emergency access accounts), or by modifying membership in the policy's security group.
  • Ensure users are registered for multifactor authentication so they can complete self‑remediation when prompted.
  • If you need assistance, submit a support request: Technical → Microsoft Entra Sign‑In and Multi‑Factor Authentication → Conditional Access → Microsoft‑managed

Learn more:

  • Microsoft-managed Conditional Access policies for enhanced security
  • Require risk remediation for high-risk users
  • User self-remediation with Microsoft Entra ID Protection
  • What are risk detections?

Compliance considerations

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.
